paragraphs.title: The Value of a Good Name, Prudence, and Education

easy.explanation: Proverbs 22:1 says, “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches.”
easy.q: What is better to choose than great riches?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “The LORD is the maker of them all.”
easy.q: Who is the maker of both the rich and the poor?

easy.explanation: The prudent man “foreseeth the evil, and hideth himself.”
easy.q: What does a prudent man do when he foresees evil?

medium.explanation: Verse 4 connects humility with “the fear of the LORD.”
medium.q: What is connected with humility in verse 4?

answers: A person who goes on into danger
medium.explanation: The simple pass on into danger and are punished, unlike the prudent man.
medium.q: What does the word “simple” describe in verse 3?

answers: He will not depart from it when old
He will learn only about money
medium.explanation: Verse 6 says that when the child is old, “he will not depart from it.”
medium.q: What is the purpose of training up a child in the proper way?

answers: A good name and loving favour are preferred to riches
challenge.explanation: The verse values a good name and loving favour above silver, gold, and great riches.
challenge.q: What comparison does verse 1 make between reputation and wealth?

answers: The LORD made both of them
challenge.explanation: Verse 2 teaches that both rich and poor are made by the LORD.
challenge.q: What can be concluded from the meeting of the rich and poor?

answers: Humility and reverence, avoiding danger, and teaching a child
challenge.explanation: These verses discuss humility, prudence, and training a child.
challenge.q: Which sequence of ideas appears in verses 4–6?

paragraphs.title: Wealth, Injustice, Generosity, and Avoiding the Mocker

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The rich ruleth over the poor.”
easy.q: Who rules over whom according to verse 7?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “He that soweth iniquity shall reap vanity.”
easy.q: What shall the person who sows iniquity reap?

answers: The person with a bountiful eye
The person who insults the poor
easy.explanation: The bountiful person is blessed because he gives his bread to the poor.

answers: The borrower is servant to the lender
medium.explanation: Verse 7 says, “the borrower is servant to the lender.”
medium.q: What relationship between borrowing and service is stated?

medium.explanation: The person with a bountiful eye gives bread to the poor, showing generosity.
medium.q: What does “a bountiful eye” describe in this context?

medium.explanation: Verse 10 says that contention goes out and strife and reproach cease.
medium.q: What happens when the scorner is cast out?

answers: The wrongdoing returns with a destructive harvest
challenge.explanation: The one who sows iniquity reaps vanity, and the rod of his anger shall fail.
challenge.q: What moral result is presented for sowing iniquity?

answers: The generous person brings blessing, while the scorner brings strife
challenge.explanation: Generosity blesses the giver, while removing the scorner ends contention and reproach.
challenge.q: How are the bountiful person and the scorner contrasted?

answers: The borrower depends on the lender
The lender depends on the poor
The rich depends on the borrower
challenge.explanation: Calling the borrower a servant of the lender emphasizes his dependence.
challenge.q: What social dependence is described in verse 7?

paragraphs.title: A Pure Heart, Divine Oversight, Laziness, and Folly

answers: The person who loves pureness of heart
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says that the king shall be the friend of one who loves pureness of heart.
easy.q: Who shall have the king as his friend?

easy.explanation: The slothful man says, “There is a lion without.”
easy.q: What excuse does the slothful man give?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child.”
easy.q: What is bound in the heart of a child?

medium.explanation: Verse 12 says, “The eyes of the LORD preserve knowledge.”
medium.q: What do the eyes of the LORD preserve?

medium.explanation: The mouth of strange women is compared to a deep pit.
medium.q: What does “a deep pit” describe in verse 14?

medium.explanation: Verse 15 says, “the rod of correction shall drive it far from him.”
medium.q: What drives foolishness far from a child?

answers: The pure-hearted person gains favour, while the transgressor’s words are overthrown
The transgressor gains favour while the pure-hearted person fails
challenge.explanation: The pure-hearted person receives the king’s friendship, while God overthrows the transgressor’s words.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the pure-hearted person and the transgressor?

answers: He uses fear as an excuse to avoid action
challenge.explanation: His claim about a lion outside is an excuse for refusing to go out and work.
challenge.q: What does the slothful man’s excuse reveal about him?

answers: Both actions can ultimately lead to want
Only giving to the poor causes want
challenge.explanation: Verse 16 warns that both oppressing the poor to gain riches and giving to the rich can lead to want.
challenge.q: What warning is given about oppressing the poor and giving to the rich?

paragraphs.title: Listening to Wisdom and Building Trust in God

easy.explanation: Verse 17 says, “Bow down thine ear, and hear the words of the wise.”
easy.q: To what should the listener incline his ear?

easy.explanation: Verse 18 speaks of keeping the words “within thee.”
easy.q: Where should the words of wisdom be kept?

easy.explanation: Verse 19 says, “That thy trust may be in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom should the person’s trust be?

answers: They should be hidden from everyone
medium.explanation: The words are to be kept within so that they become fitted in the lips.
medium.q: What should be done with the words of the wise besides hearing them?

medium.explanation: The passage emphasizes the certainty and truthfulness of the words being taught.
medium.q: What does “the words of truth” refer to?

answers: Answering truthfully those who send questions
medium.explanation: Verse 21 says the learner may answer the words of truth to those who send him.
medium.q: What ability results from learning these teachings?

answers: Hearing, internalizing, speaking, and answering with truth
Hearing, forgetting, and refusing to answer
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from hearing wisdom to keeping it within, speaking it, and giving truthful answers.
challenge.q: What process is described in verses 17–21?

answers: Learning wisdom helps establish trust in the LORD
Wisdom replaces trust in the LORD
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 presents the teaching as a means of directing the learner’s trust toward the LORD.
challenge.q: How is wisdom related to trust in the LORD?

answers: They are internalized and ready to be spoken properly
challenge.explanation: The phrase describes wisdom being stored within and expressed clearly.
challenge.q: What does it mean for the words to be “fitted in thy lips”?

paragraphs.title: Protecting the Vulnerable and Being Careful with Associations and Commitments

easy.explanation: Verse 22 says, “Rob not the poor, because he is poor.”
easy.q: Whom does the passage warn people not to rob?

easy.explanation: Verse 24 warns against friendship with an angry or furious man.
easy.q: With whom should a person not make friendship?

answers: A commitment that could cause him to lose his bed
easy.explanation: The passage warns against becoming surety for a debt that cannot be paid.
easy.q: What should a person avoid if he has nothing to pay?

answers: He will give the oppressor riches
medium.explanation: Verse 23 says, “the LORD will plead their cause.”
medium.q: What will the LORD do for the poor who are oppressed?

answers: Do not form a close association
medium.explanation: The command warns against close association with an angry person.
medium.q: What does “make no friendship” mean in this passage?

answers: He may learn the man’s ways and fall into a snare
He may become more closely attached to him
medium.explanation: Verse 25 warns that learning the angry man’s ways can become a snare to the soul.
medium.q: Why should a person avoid a furious man?

answers: God pleads the cause of those who are oppressed
challenge.explanation: The LORD personally pleads the cause of the poor and afflicted.
challenge.q: What connection is made between harming the poor and God’s protection?

answers: Avoid relationships and commitments that can become snares
Stay close to every angry person
challenge.explanation: Both warnings urge practical caution against traps that can harm one’s life.
challenge.q: What principle is shared by the warnings about anger and surety?

challenge.explanation: Verse 27 asks why the lender should take away the debtor’s bed from under him.
challenge.q: What may be the cost of guaranteeing a debt without the ability to pay?

easy.explanation: Verse 28 says, “Remove not the ancient landmark.”
The verse refers to the landmarks “which thy fathers have set.”
Verse 29 says a diligent person “shall stand before kings.”
easy.q: Where shall a diligent person stand?

answers: The boundaries were set by the fathers and should be respected
The boundaries were set by lazy people
The boundaries have no historical importance
medium.explanation: The verse specifically identifies the fathers as those who established the landmarks.
medium.q: What connection does verse 28 make with earlier generations?

medium.explanation: A diligent person is careful, energetic, and committed to his business.
medium.q: What does “diligent” mean in this context?

medium.explanation: The verse links diligence in business with appearing before kings.
medium.q: What is the result of diligence according to verse 29?

answers: Respecting established boundaries while advancing through diligence
Gaining wealth by oppressing the poor
challenge.explanation: The passage honors both preserving rightful boundaries and progressing through diligent work.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between the two final verses?

answers: The diligent person rises to a respected position rather than remaining among the lowly
The diligent person avoids all people
The diligent person loses his employment
challenge.explanation: The phrase contrasts the diligent person’s standing before kings with remaining before mean men.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from not standing before “mean men”?

challenge.explanation: Both verses commend responsible conduct: preserving what is right and working diligently.
challenge.q: What shared value appears in respecting landmarks and praising diligence?
